blocks.text: The client manages around 4,800 apartments with nine property managers and three assistants. A shared mailbox was receiving about 140 mails a day, mixing fault reports, water damage, sauna bookings and payment questions. Assistants triaged by hand.

The team built the smallest useful version: a classifier that labels incoming mails into six categories with an urgency flag, and generates a suggested reply draft in the shared Outlook mailbox. Nothing is sent automatically. Urgent items trigger an SMS to the on-call person and are highlighted. A keyword fallback runs if the language model is unavailable.

In a two-week pilot with two of three assistants, median first response time moved from 26 hours to 7.5 hours (measured). Assistants said triage time was roughly halved, but this was not timed. The third assistant preferred their existing method, and a pairing session was planned. A spot check found drafts with wrong apartment numbers in 2 of 20 cases, so a 'check fields' banner was added.

Data handling: no tenant data is stored outside the EU tenant, logs are kept 30 days, and a data processing agreement was signed. Results are early, come from a small pilot, and the test accuracy figures apply to historic mails rather than live traffic.

blocks.text:
A property manager with ~4,800 apartments was getting about 140 shared-inbox mails a day. Faults, water damage, sauna bookings and payments were all mixed together.

We built a small classifier that labels each mail and drafts a reply for an assistant to check. Nothing sends automatically. Urgent mails trigger an SMS to on-call.

In a two-week pilot with two assistants, median first response fell from 26 h to 7.5 h (measured). Early days, small pilot. The team is still checking drafts closely: one spot check caught wrong apartment numbers in 2 of 20.

If your shared inbox is the bottleneck, we are happy to talk through what it would take to look at it.

Client: Kallio & Lehtonen Kiinteistöt Oy
Project owner: Mikko Heikkilä
client: isännöinti, ~4 800 apts, 9 isännöitsijää + 3 assistants
- pain: shared inbox isannointi@ gets ~140 mails/day, vikailmoitukset (faults), vesivahingot, saunavuorot, maksukysymykset all mixed
- baseline: assistants triage by hand, first response time median 26 h (pulled from ticket export, 2 months)
- urgent ones (vesivuoto!) sometimes sit >1 working day. 3 cases last quarter per Laura (not verified)
- smallest build: classifier (6 categories + urgency flag) via LLM on incoming mails -> label + suggested reply draft in Outlook shared mailbox. NO auto-send
- urgent = SMS to on-call + highlighted. Kept rules simple, keyword fallback if LLM down
- wk2 test on 400 historic mails: category acc 88% vs Laura's labels, urgency recall 94% (missed 2 of 33, both vague wording)
- drafts: assistants edit ~half, 'sävy liian jäykkä' -> prompt tuned, tone examples from their own sent mails
- pilot wk3-4 w/ 2 assistants. median first response 26 h -> 7.5 h (measured, 2 wks, summer-ish low season? no, Nov, ok)
- time on triage ~ 'halved' per assistants, not timed
- GDPR: no tenant data stored outside EU tenant, logs 30 d. DPA signed
- adoption: 2/3 assistants use daily, 3rd 'prefers own way' -> pair session next mo
- risk: drafts copy-pasted w/o reading? spot check 20 -> 2 had wrong apt number. added 'check fields' banner
